title: Vehicle Retail Registrations - All Segments (FADA)
description: Monthly retail registrations (units) of all new vehicles in India - two-wheelers, three-wheelers, passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles and tractors - as compiled by the dealers' federation FADA from VAHAN. Unlike manufacturers' dispatches (SIAM), this is sales to end customers, so it is a cleaner read of consumer and fleet demand and is used in activity monitors as a timely proxy for discretionary spending, rural demand and credit conditions. FADA publishes in the first week after month-end.
source: FADA (Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations), monthly vehicle retail data press releases (VAHAN-based)

qna.question: What does this series measure?
qna.answer: Number of new vehicles registered at regional transport offices in a month (all five segments together), as reported in FADA's monthly press release.^It counts registrations (retail to the end customer) and not factory dispatches to dealers, so it avoids channel stuffing and inventory swings that affect dispatch numbers.

qna.question: How should I read it?
qna.answer: Registrations are strongly seasonal: peaks around Navratri/Diwali (Oct-Nov), the March financial-year end and wedding/harvest months, and troughs in monsoon and Shraadh periods. Compare with the same month a year earlier (YoY view) and watch festival timing shifts between months.^Two-wheelers are roughly 70 per cent of units, so the total mostly tracks rural and low-income demand; passenger vehicles dominate in value.

qna.question: What are the caveats and revisions?
qna.answer: FADA's coverage of RTOs was incomplete in 2019-2022 and the latest month is collated a few days after month-end, so FADA restates earlier months upward in later releases (by roughly 5-8 per cent for Sep 2025, for instance). This series uses the restated year-ago figure from the next year's release where available, so YoY growth matches FADA's own published growth rates; the latest 12 months are as first released.^Tax/regulatory changes (BS-VI, GST changes, subsidy rules) and festival calendars cause large base effects, so single-month growth rates can mislead.

note: Values are VAHAN-based registrations ('retail') collated by FADA for the RTOs it can access; coverage of states changed over time (e.g. Telangana, Lakshadweep and some others were missing early on, Kerala added Dec 2019, Wheeled construction equipment added to the total in 2026), and FADA restates earlier months (by up to ~5-8 per cent in 2025-26) in later releases. To keep growth rates like-for-like, each month's own-release figure is replaced by the restated year-ago figure printed in the following year's release when one exists, so the latest 12 months are as first released and are likely to be revised up. The 'All vehicles' total includes tractors from Jan 2020 only.
